anomalies.observed: R48 is valued "24k" in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part ("125mW ... ±5% 24Ω 0805", MPN FRC0805J240TSD, where "240" denotes 24Ω).
anomalies.expected: A 24Ω resistor, matching the value field, the description and the MPN, since the part is a 24Ω 0805 chip resistor.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R48") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: The value in the schematic and simulation differs from the ordered part by a factor of 1000, so the load or bleed path across the VOUTP/VOUTN rail will not behave as designed.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three Ethernet/activity LEDs D8 (green), D40 (green) and D45 (yellow) are on net /NET0198 and on no other node. Nothing supplies the anode net, so the anodes are floating.
anomalies.expected: LED anodes should be tied to a supply such as +3V3, as the other status LEDs are (D15 and D17 via R76 and R99 to +3V3). The cathodes are driven low by the CM4 nLED/activity outputs through R42, R75 and R13.
anomalies.impact: The three link/activity indicators cannot light, since their anodes have no supply path. The board's network status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: The 4-pin I2C OLED header J7 has +5V on pin 1 and +3V3 on pin 2. No pin of J7 is on GND, so the OLED has no ground connection. Its two supply pins sit on different rails.
anomalies.expected: A 4-pin I2C OLED header (compare J14, which has +3V3, SCL, SDA and GND) should have GND on one pin and a single supply on another.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "J7") (value "I2C OLED") ... (note "128x64 Pixel SH1106 I2C OLED widely available on Amazon or Aliexpress etc")

anomalies.impact: The OLED has no ground reference and may not function, or may be damaged by being fed from two different rails through its own supply circuitry.
